t:
(a) Study Requirement.—The Secretary of Defense, acting through the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics in coordination with the service acquisition executives of each military department, shall conduct a study on revisions to requirements relating to Selected Acquisition Reports, as set forth in section 2432 of title 10, United States Code. 
    (b) Matters Covered.—The study required under subsection (a) shall—
        (1) focus on incorporating into the Selected Acquisition Report those elements of program progress that the Department of Defense considers most relevant to evaluating the performance and progress of major defense acquisition programs, with particular reference to the cost estimates and program schedule established when a major defense acquisition program receives Milestone B approval; 
        (2) address the need to ensure that data provided through the Selected Acquisition Report is consistent with data provided through internal Department of Defense reporting systems for management purposes; and 
        (3) include any recommendations to add to, modify, or delete elements of the Selected Acquisition Report, consistent with the findings of the study.  
    (c) Report.—Not later than March 1, 2007, the Secretary shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a report on the results of the study, including such recommendations as the Secretary considers appropriate.

fable.w: The tempting reading treats the "in coordination with" language and the report requirement as participation. However, the coordination is with service acquisition executives of the military departments, who are federal officials, and the report goes to congressional Armed Services Committees, which are also inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, and the section concerns a study rather than an outside-informed decision.
fable.s: acting through the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics in coordination with the service acquisition executives of each military department

qwen_block.w: The section requires a study conducted by federal officials (Secretary of Defense, Under Secretary, service acquisition executives) and a report to Congress. All actors involved are inside the federal government. There is no consultation with outside parties, public comment period, or advisory board with non-federal members.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of Defense, acting through the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics in coordination with the service acquisition executives of each military department, shall conduct a study

opus.w: The only coordination is among Defense Department officials (the Under Secretary and the military departments' service acquisition executives), so it stays within the federal government. The report goes to the Senate and House Armed Services Committees, which are also part of the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, so the procedural wording does not count as participation.
opus.s: The Secretary of Defense, acting through the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics in coordination with the service acquisition executives of each military department, shall conduct a study
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** The section says "in coordination with" and requires a report to the Armed Services Committees, so it can look like a consultation process.

**Why that fails:** Everyone involved is inside the federal government. The Secretary of Defense, the Under Secretary, and the military departments' service acquisition executives are all federal officials. The Armed Services Committees belong to Congress. Nobody outside the government takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires a study conducted by federal officials (Secretary of Defense, Under Secretary, service acquisition executives) and a report to Congress. All actors involved are inside the federal government. There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities. Intra-governmental coordination is not participation.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of Defense, acting through the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology, and Logistics in coordination with the service acquisition executives of each military department, shall conduct a study
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "coordination with the service acquisition executives" constitutes participation because it involves multiple parties. However, the Under Secretary of Defense and the service acquisition executives are all federal officials/employees. Coordination entirely within the federal government is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
